original_value: Electric energy consumption forecasting is an interesting, challenging, and important issue in energy management and equipment efficiency improvement. Existing approaches are predictive models that have the ability to predict for a specific profile, i.e., a time series of a whole building or an individual household in a smart building. In practice, there are many profiles in each smart building, which leads to time-consuming and expensive system resources. Therefore, this study develops a robust framework for the Multiple Electric Energy Consumption forecasting (MEC) of a smart building using Transfer Learning and Long Short-Term Memory (TLL), the so-called MEC-TLL framework. In this framework, we first employ a k-means clustering algorithm to cluster the daily load demand of many profiles in the training set. In this phase, we also perform Silhouette analysis to specify the optimal number of clusters for the experimental datasets. Next, this study develops the MEC training algorithm, which utilizes a cluster-based strategy for transfer learning the Long Short-Term Memory models to reduce the computational time. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to compare the computational time and different performance metrics for multiple electric energy consumption forecasting on two smart buildings in South Korea. The experimental results indicate that our proposed approach is capable of economical overheads while achieving superior performances. Therefore, the proposed approach can be applied effectively for intelligent energy management in smart buildings.

result.paraphrase: Electric energy consumption forecasting is an important, challenging, and interesting problem in energy management and improving equipment efficiency. Current methods are predictive models that can forecast a particular profile, namely a time series for an entire building or for a single household in a smart building. In real deployments, each smart building contains many profiles, making the system resource requirements expensive and time-consuming. To address this, the study proposes a robust Multiple Electric Energy Consumption forecasting framework for a smart building based on Transfer Learning and Long Short-Term Memory, called MEC-TLL. The framework begins by using k-means clustering to group the daily load demand of multiple profiles in the training set. Silhouette analysis is also applied at this stage to determine the optimal number of clusters for the experimental datasets. Next, the MEC training algorithm is developed, using a cluster-based transfer learning strategy for Long Short-Term Memory models to reduce computation time. Finally, extensive experiments compare computation time and various performance metrics for multiple electric energy consumption forecasting on two smart buildings in South Korea. The results show that the proposed method achieves superior performance with low overhead, indicating that it can be applied effectively to intelligent energy management in smart buildings.
